g.content:
<UserObject label="<font style="font-size: 18px; color: rgb(51, 51, 51);"><b style="">?</b></font>" help="Kernel Activity (what runtime instrumentation sees)

A container process is a normal host process: every exec, file open and connection goes through the host kernel. Runtime security tools (Tetragon, Falco) attach eBPF programs to kernel hooks and read the activity there, without an agent in the pod and regardless of what the image contains.
Each event carries the task's cgroup ID and namespace IDs, which the tool maps to container, Pod, namespace and workload via the container runtime (CRI) and the Kubernetes API.

<b>Sources</b>
- process-exec: execve/execveat, tracepoint sched_process_exec, LSM hook bprm_check_security. Binary, arguments, UID/GID, capabilities, cwd.
- process-tree: built by the tool from fork (wake_up_new_task, sched_process_fork) and exit (acct_process, sched_process_exit). Parent chain back to containerd-shim/runc, so a shell spawned by a web server stands out.
- syscalls: raw tracepoints sys_enter/sys_exit (Falco's base source), or kprobes on single syscalls such as __x64_sys_setuid or __x64_sys_ptrace (Tetragon TracingPolicy).
- network: tcp_connect, inet_csk_accept, tcp_sendmsg, udp_sendmsg, tcp_close, tracepoint sock:inet_sock_set_state. 5-tuple per process, not only per pod.
- socket: security_socket_create, security_socket_bind, security_socket_listen, security_socket_connect. Unexpected listeners, raw and packet sockets.
- file-access: security_file_open, security_file_permission, security_mmap_file, fd_install. Reads of /etc/shadow, ServiceAccount tokens, host paths.
- file-change: security_path_unlink, security_path_rename, security_path_chmod, security_path_truncate, security_inode_setattr. Dropped binaries, changed configs.

<b>Hook types</b>
- Tracepoints are a stable kernel interface.
- Kprobes/fentry can hook any kernel function, but names and arguments change between kernel versions.
- LSM BPF hooks (CONFIG_BPF_LSM) and functions that allow error injection can also deny: Tetragon can override the return value or send SIGKILL in the kernel, before the action completes.

Falco is syscall-based: file and network activity are read from the syscalls. Tetragon hooks the kernel functions behind them, which avoids TOCTOU gaps in syscall arguments.

<b>Limits</b>
- Kata, gVisor and VMs run the workload on their own guest kernel or sandbox: the host's eBPF sees the sandbox, not the process inside.
- Hooking every syscall or file read costs CPU. Filter in the kernel (Tetragon selectors, Falco's event set) and send on only what matters.
- Events stay on the node; forward them to a central system to correlate and keep them." tags="level-3 info Node Node.RuntimeSecurity _ _.Area _.Area.Cluster _.Area.Deployment _.Area.Pod _.Area.Container _.Area.Process _.Area.KernelActivity" slug="KernelActivity" help.json.process_exec_event="# Tetragon process_exec event (trimmed): binary started from /tmp in pod shop/cache-warmer
{
 "process_exec": {
 "process": {
 "exec_id": "d29ya2VyLTA1OjE4MzQ2MjkxMDQ1MTIyOjQ4NzMx",
 "pid": 48731,
 "uid": 0,
 "cwd": "/",
 "binary": "/tmp/.kworkerd",
 "arguments": "-d t.cdnx.example",
 "flags": "execve rootcwd",
 "start_time": "2026-10-14T03:41:07.512345678Z",
 "pod": {
 "namespace": "shop",
 "name": "cache-warmer",
 "container": {
 "id": "containerd://1a84a5803de42872c9ab3398fc81d59a1d44fc21b01dd1e73e085046ef0f0114",
 "name": "cache-warmer",
 "image": {
 "id": "docker.io/library/debian@sha256:9d4bf569e737266d93655e630c601e8810000116f0681e70f489c347717bd590",
 "name": "docker.io/library/debian:latest"
 }
 },
 "workload": "cache-warmer"
 },
 "parent_exec_id": "d29ya2VyLTA1OjE4MzQ2MjkwOTEzMzg1OjQ4NzE0"
 },
 "parent": {
 "pid": 48714,
 "binary": "/bin/sh"
 }
 },
 "node_name": "worker-05",
 "time": "2026-10-14T03:41:07.512345678Z"
}"/>
g.data-help: Kernel Activity (what runtime instrumentation sees) A container process is a normal host process: every exec, file open and connection goes through the host kernel. Runtime security tools (Tetragon, Falco) attach eBPF programs to kernel hooks and read the activity there, without an agent in the pod and regardless of what the image contains. Each event carries the task's cgroup ID and namespace IDs, which the tool maps to container, Pod, namespace and workload via the container runtime (CRI) and the Kubernetes API. Sources - process-exec: execve/execveat, tracepoint sched_process_exec, LSM hook bprm_check_security. Binary, arguments, UID/GID, capabilities, cwd. - process-tree: built by the tool from fork (wake_up_new_task, sched_process_fork) and exit (acct_process, sched_process_exit). Parent chain back to containerd-shim/runc, so a shell spawned by a web server stands out. - syscalls: raw tracepoints sys_enter/sys_exit (Falco's base source), or kprobes on single syscalls such as __x64_sys_setuid or __x64_sys_ptrace (Tetragon TracingPolicy). - network: tcp_connect, inet_csk_accept, tcp_sendmsg, udp_sendmsg, tcp_close, tracepoint sock:inet_sock_set_state. 5-tuple per process, not only per pod. - socket: security_socket_create, security_socket_bind, security_socket_listen, security_socket_connect. Unexpected listeners, raw and packet sockets. - file-access: security_file_open, security_file_permission, security_mmap_file, fd_install. Reads of /etc/shadow, ServiceAccount tokens, host paths. - file-change: security_path_unlink, security_path_rename, security_path_chmod, security_path_truncate, security_inode_setattr. Dropped binaries, changed configs. Hook types - Tracepoints are a stable kernel interface. - Kprobes/fentry can hook any kernel function, but names and arguments change between kernel versions. - LSM BPF hooks (CONFIG_BPF_LSM) and functions that allow error injection can also deny: Tetragon can override the return value or send SIGKILL in the kernel, before the action completes. Falco is syscall-based: file and network activity are read from the syscalls. Tetragon hooks the kernel functions behind them, which avoids TOCTOU gaps in syscall arguments. Limits - Kata, gVisor and VMs run the workload on their own guest kernel or sandbox: the host's eBPF sees the sandbox, not the process inside. - Hooking every syscall or file read costs CPU. Filter in the kernel (Tetragon selectors, Falco's event set) and send on only what matters. - Events stay on the node; forward them to a central system to correlate and keep them.
